chapter: Package shows, Miami and the USO
title: A far-out trumpeter and Miles Davis's weeks
summary: Miles Davis plays three weeks with him; A.G. still on drums.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Way out, way out; not Dizzy Gillespie? Someone like him?
Yeah.
It wasn't Miles Davis?
No, Miles played with me for a while though.
Miles played with you?
Yeah.
When did Miles play with you?
I forget what year it was.
How long did Miles play with you?
About three weeks.
I can't imagine him.
He didn't play way out then.
No, I know he didn't. This would probably be not too long after you came out of the service--not the service--'46 probably.
He came down to see me in the sixties, when I was getting ready to go overseas.
I never knew he played with you.
He played with me for about three weeks.
Here in New York probably?
Yeah.
It must have been in somewhere like the One Hundred Club.
It wasn't in the One Hundred Club, because one of the things about the One Hundred Club, I was broadcasting coast to coast four nights a week, Billy Daniels was a
Norma Shepherd.
Norma Shepherd; it was some club.
They had good clubs on the west side like that for years.
That was some club, we did some business.
So you're saying a far out trumpet player, you say he had his own band?
Something pertaining to color.
Who was playing drums, was A.G. still playing drums with you or not?
Yeah, A.G. was still on drums.
Snead was still with you?
No.
So mostly it was different guys, New York guys?
Yeah.
